Quick reference

The regex cheatsheet

Everything Relay's parser understands, in one place. This is JavaScript (ECMAScript) flavour — the same engine that runs in the lab. Click any pattern to try it.

Character classes

.Any char except newline (any char with s flag)
\d \DDigit [0-9] / non-digit
\w \WWord char [A-Za-z0-9_] / non-word
\s \SWhitespace / non-whitespace
[abc]Any one of a, b, or c
[^abc]Any char NOT a, b, or c
[a-z]A range: any lowercase letter
[\d.]Shorthands combine inside a class

Anchors & boundaries

^Start of string (start of line with m)
$End of string (end of line with m)
\bWord boundary
\BNot a word boundary

Quantifiers

*0 or more (greedy)
+1 or more (greedy)
?0 or 1 (optional)
{n}Exactly n times
{n,}n or more times
{n,m}Between n and m times
*? +? ??Lazy variants — as few as possible

Groups & references

( … )Capturing group (numbered)
(?: … )Non-capturing group
(?<name> … )Named capturing group
\1 \2Backreference to group 1, 2…
\k<name>Backreference to a named group
a|bAlternation — match a OR b

Lookaround

(?= … )Positive lookahead — followed by
(?! … )Negative lookahead — not followed by
(?<= … )Positive lookbehind — preceded by
(?<! … )Negative lookbehind — not preceded by

Escapes & literals

\. \* \\Escape a metacharacter to match it literally
\n \r \tNewline, carriage return, tab
\xHHChar by 2-digit hex code (\x41 = A)
\uHHHHChar by 4-digit hex code (é = é)
\u{H…}Code point (needs u flag)
\p{…}Unicode property (needs u flag)

Flags

gGlobal — find all matches, not just the first
iIgnore case
mMultiline — ^/$ match line edges
sdotAll — . matches newlines too
uUnicode — full code-point semantics
ySticky — anchored at lastIndex

Replacement tokens

$&The whole match
$1 $2Capture group 1, 2…
$<name>Named capture group
$`Text before the match
$'Text after the match
$$A literal dollar sign

Gotchas & performance

  • Catastrophic backtracking. Nested quantifiers over overlapping patterns — e.g. (a+)+$ against "aaaaaaX" — can explode into exponential work. Relay caps each run at 250ms and warns if it bails.
  • Greedy vs. lazy. <.*> on <a><b> grabs the whole thing; <.*?> stops at the first >.
  • Escape your dots. 192.168.0.1 — the unescaped . matches any char. Use \. for a literal dot.
  • Zero-width matches. Patterns like \b or (?=…) match an empty string; Relay marks them with a thin caret in the test text.
  • The g flag and lastIndex. A global regex is stateful between .exec() calls. Relay creates a fresh one each run to avoid surprises.
